questions.first: I regret not studying harder at school.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past perfect is used to express regret about something in the past.

questions.first: I managed to finish the report on time.
questions.explanation: 'Be able to' + infinitive is an alternative way of expressing 'managed to'.

questions.first: Although it was raining, we went for a walk.
questions.after: the rain, we went for a walk.
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' + noun phrase expresses the same contrast as 'although' + clause.

questions.first: It is possible that the train was delayed by weather.
questions.explanation: 'Must have been' expresses a confident deduction about something in the past.

questions.first: I would prefer to stay at home tonight.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' + bare infinitive expresses a preference, like 'would prefer to'.

questions.first: I don't do as much exercise now as I did when I was younger.
questions.after: do more exercise when I was younger.
questions.explanation: 'Used to' + infinitive describes a past habit that no longer happens.
